ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. 'Too much sugar is bad for your teeth.' Sugar is (1 mark)
   A. countable
   B. a verb
   C. a plural noun
   D. uncountable

2. Which sentence compares Kevin and Musa correctly? (1 mark)
   A. Kevin is tall than Musa.
   B. Kevin is more taller than Musa.
   C. Kevin is tallest than Musa.
   D. Kevin is taller than Musa.

3. Which question is inferential? (1 mark)
   A. Where is the barbershop?
   B. What day did Baraka visit the barber?
   C. How did Omondi feel at the start of the story?
   D. What did the barber put into his razor?

4. In a readers' theatre, learners (1 mark)
   A. read a story aloud with different parts
   B. build a stage from wood
   C. sing without words
   D. draw pictures only

5. What is the negative form of 'We are shouting'? (1 mark)
   A. We do not shouting.
   B. We are not shouting.
   C. We not are shouting.
   D. We are no shouting.

6. In which tense is a description usually written? (1 mark)
   A. Command form
   B. Present tense
   C. Future perfect
   D. Past perfect

7. Which sentence uses the correct participle of 'eat'? (1 mark)
   A. She has ate her lunch.
   B. She have eaten her lunch.
   C. She has eaten her lunch.
   D. She has eating her lunch.

8. Which word in this sentence is the adverb? 'The nurse spoke gently.' (1 mark)
   A. nurse
   B. spoke
   C. The
   D. gently

9. Which of these is a reference material? (1 mark)
   A. A dictionary
   B. A letter
   C. A song
   D. A storybook

10. Which online reading habit is safe? (1 mark)
   A. Visiting any page a stranger suggests
   B. Clicking every advert
   C. Reading only pages approved by a teacher or parent
   D. Giving your address to a website

11. A word has two meanings in the dictionary. What should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Use the last meaning always
   B. Ignore both
   C. Choose the meaning that fits your sentence
   D. Use the first meaning always

12. Which word begins with /v/? (1 mark)
   A. window
   B. vegetables
   C. weed
   D. wheat

13. Which is written correctly? (1 mark)
   A. we climbed mount elgon
   B. We climbed Mount Elgon.
   C. We climbed mount elgon,
   D. we climbed mount elgon!

14. How long is a descriptive composition at this level? (1 mark)
   A. 10 to 20 words
   B. 200 to 300 words
   C. 500 words
   D. 80 to 100 words

15. What is fluency? (1 mark)
   A. Reading only one word
   B. Not reading
   C. Reading smoothly with few stops
   D. Reading very loudly

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Explain why flies are dangerous to health. (2 marks)

17. Correct the paragraph: 'last friday our class visited the museum. mr. juma told us about kenya.' (4 marks)

18. What lesson does the poem 'The Whistle' teach about winning and losing? (2 marks)

19. Explain why we say 'a university' but 'an umbrella'. (3 marks)

20. Write one sentence in the present progressive and one in the past progressive about a farm. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — uncountable
   We cannot count sugar one by one.

2. D — Kevin is taller than Musa.
   Use the er form with than.

3. C — How did Omondi feel at the start of the story?
   You work out his feelings from clues.

4. A — read a story aloud with different parts
   Each reader takes a part and reads the lines.

5. B — We are not shouting.
   Not comes after are.

6. B — Present tense
   Descriptions often say what something is like now.

7. C — She has eaten her lunch.
   Has + eaten.

8. D — gently
   'Gently' tells how she spoke.

9. A — A dictionary
   A dictionary is used to look up spelling and meaning, so it is a reference book.

10. C — Reading only pages approved by a teacher or parent
   Approved pages keep you safe online.

11. C — Choose the meaning that fits your sentence
   Read all meanings and choose the one that matches how the word is used.

12. B — vegetables
   'Vegetables' begins with /v/, said with the top teeth on the lower lip.

13. B — We climbed Mount Elgon.
   The first word and the mountain name need capitals, and a statement ends with a full stop.

14. D — 80 to 100 words
   The task calls for 80 to 100 words.

15. C — Reading smoothly with few stops
   Fluent readers read smoothly.

SECTION B
----
16. (2 marks)
   Answer: Flies land on waste and then on food, so they carry germs to the food we eat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for waste then food and 1 mark for germs spreading.

17. (4 marks)
   Answer: Last Friday our class visited the museum. Mr. Juma told us about Kenya.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for Last Friday, Mr. Juma, Kenya and correct full stops.

18. (2 marks)
   Answer: To be a good sport: lose without crying, shake hands with the other team and say 'Good try'.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the lesson and 1 for a reason from the poem.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: Both start with the letter u, but university starts with the consonant sound 'yoo', so it takes a. Umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so it takes an. We choose by sound, not by letter.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each example and 1 mark for the sound rule.

20. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: The farmer is digging the field. The cows were eating grass.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each sentence: 1 for the correct form of be, 1 for the -ing verb.
